sections.title: SciELO XML Conversion for Scholarly Publishing

lead.text: Scholarly articles contain structured information that must remain meaningful beyond the way it appears on a printed or digital page.
Titles, authors, affiliations, abstracts, keywords, references, tables, figures and other article components may need to be identified using appropriate XML elements.
SciELO XML markup supports this structured representation of scholarly content.

blocks.text: The SciELO Publishing Schema is a set of XML specifications developed for SciELO publishing workflows. It builds on the Journal Article Tag Suite (JATS) and introduces SciELO-specific requirements for article structure, metadata and content markup.
JATS and SciELO PS are related, but they are not interchangeable specifications. A general JATS XML file may need additional preparation or changes to meet an applicable SciELO requirement.
EPUBTRANS can assess eligible scholarly content for conversion and markup according to the specified SciELO workflow.
The schema version, journal requirements, validation rules and expected deliverables must be confirmed before production.

lead.text: SciELO XML production involves identifying and representing the structural and semantic components of scholarly articles.
Depending on the source material and agreed requirements, the service may include the following activities.

blocks.text: Preparation of article content using XML elements appropriate to the required SciELO Publishing Schema.
Typical components include:

items: Article titles and other front matter
Paragraphs, lists and other body content

blocks.text: The exact tagging structure depends on the article type and applicable specification.
Preparation of XML metadata from information supplied or approved by the publisher.
This may include journal identifiers, article titles, contributor information, affiliations, publication dates, article identifiers, abstracts and language information.
We identify missing or inconsistent source metadata for clarification rather than inventing information that has not been supplied.
Structuring reference lists and bibliographic information using the required XML elements.
References may contain contributor names, titles, journal details, volume and issue information, publication years, page ranges and identifiers.
The accuracy and completeness of reference data depend on the supplied sources and any separately agreed editorial or bibliographic verification.
XML markup for tables, figures, captions, labels and associated content.
Complex tables, nested elements, image relationships and supplementary assets may need individual assessment.
The project specification determines whether artwork preparation, file conversion or correction of source content is included.
Preparation of mathematical and technical content within the specified XML structure.
Where applicable, mathematical expressions may involve MathML or other approved representations.
Equations, symbols and specialist notation can require additional source review and markup decisions.
Support for a particular mathematical representation or toolchain must be confirmed for the project.
Inclusion of supplied identifiers, such as Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs), in the appropriate article or reference metadata fields where required.
XML markup of an existing DOI is different from DOI registration or depositing metadata with Crossref.
Registration, assignment, verification or external submission activities are separate unless expressly included in the agreement.
Review and correction of XML markup based on agreed production feedback, revised source information or identified technical issues.
Revision rounds, error-resolution responsibilities and resubmission requirements are defined as part of the project scope.

sections.title: SciELO XML vs General JATS XML

lead.text: SciELO XML and general JATS XML serve related structured-publishing purposes, but the production requirements are not necessarily identical.

blocks.text: JATS provides standardized XML structures for scholarly journal articles and related publication information.
Different publishers and repositories may specify different JATS tag sets, versions or implementation rules.
SciELO XML follows the applicable SciELO Publishing Schema requirements and any additional rules established for the intended SciELO publishing workflow.
This means a JATS-based article may require additional markup, metadata adjustments or validation before it meets the specified SciELO requirements.
When requesting XML conversion, publishers should identify the target specification and intended downstream use.

sections.title: What Affects SciELO XML Project Scope & Schedule?

blocks.text: Editable, clearly organized manuscripts may require a different level of preparation from PDFs, scanned documents or inconsistent legacy source files.
The number of figures, tables, equations, references and supplementary files can affect markup requirements.
Missing affiliations, identifiers, funding details, reference data or other required information can lead to queries and additional review.
The required SciELO schema version, journal-specific instructions and validation tools influence the production and checking process.
The number of review stages, error-correction rounds, package revisions and downstream delivery requirements can affect the overall scope.
We review these factors before discussing production estimates or schedules.

SciELO XML markup is the process of structuring scholarly article content using the XML elements and rules required by the applicable SciELO Publishing Schema. It includes article content, metadata, references and other publishing information.

groups.title: What is the difference between SciELO XML and JATS XML?

blocks.text: SciELO Publishing Schema is based on JATS but introduces SciELO-specific requirements. A general JATS XML file may not satisfy every SciELO validation or publishing requirement without additional work.

groups.title: Can EPUBTRANS convert Word articles into SciELO XML?

blocks.text: Microsoft Word is among the documented source formats for XML production. We review the article structure, metadata, figures, references and target requirements before confirming the production scope.

groups.title: Can you convert existing journal PDFs into SciELO XML?

blocks.text: PDF files can be assessed for XML conversion. Depending on the source, the work may require reconstructing article structure, extracting text and clarifying missing metadata or content relationships.

groups.title: Do you support references, tables and figures in SciELO XML?

blocks.text: These elements are included in EPUBTRANS's documented XML service scope. The exact markup and any required corrections depend on the source materials and target specification.

groups.title: Can you include DOI information in XML?

blocks.text: Existing DOI information supplied or confirmed by the publisher can be marked up according to the required specification. DOI registration or Crossref deposit services are not automatically included.

groups.title: Does EPUBTRANS provide SciELO XML validation?

blocks.text: Validation can be included according to the agreed project requirements. The applicable specification, tools, correction process and reporting expectations must be confirmed before production.

groups.title: Does successful XML validation guarantee acceptance by SciELO?

blocks.text: No. XML validation checks technical requirements within its defined scope. Acceptance by a particular journal or SciELO collection can also depend on additional editorial, administrative and submission criteria.

groups.title: Can you correct existing SciELO XML files?

blocks.text: Existing XML files can be reviewed for agreed corrections or updates. Please provide the files, validation feedback, expected output and applicable specifications for assessment.

groups.title: What do you need to prepare a SciELO XML quote?

blocks.text: Please share representative article files, approximate article volume, source formats, target SciELO requirements, available metadata and assets, validation expectations and preferred schedule.

groups.title: Is EPUBTRANS a SciELO-certified XML service provider?

blocks.text: Yes. EPUBTRANS is listed on SciELO's official directory of companies certified for XML article text tagging services according to the SciELO Publishing Schema.
You can verify EPUBTRANS's listing directly on the official SciELO website.
Certification does not eliminate the need for project-specific validation or guarantee automatic acceptance of every submitted XML package.
